topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: re-home the RPC recording hooks (recorder seam + rpc.JsonError)
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #21745 (§15 of the [op-geth decoupling doc](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md#L437-L444)). **Blocks #20266.**

op-geth adds `rpc.Recorder` / `RecordedMsg` / `RecordDone` / `WithRecorder` hooks *inside* geth's RPC client **and** server, and exports `rpc.JsonError` (unexported upstream). Three op-service foundations build on them; upstream go-ethereum offers no equivalent, so we have to own the seam.

## Scope (measured at 1657fbe)

- [`op-service/metrics/rpc_metrics.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/op-service/metrics/rpc_metrics.go#L16-L45) — `RPCMetricer.NewRecorder(name) rpc.Recorder` leaks the geth type into every service's metrics struct; [`rpcRecorder`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/op-service/metrics/rpc_metrics.go#L171-L211) emits the client *and* server RPC metrics.
- Client side: [`op-service/client.WithRPCRecorder`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/op-service/client/rpc.go#L109-L115) forwards straight into `rpc.WithRecorder` on the geth client.
- Server side: [`op-service/rpc.Handler.recorder`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/op-service/rpc/handler.go#L46) / [`WithRPCRecorder`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/op-service/rpc/handler_options.go#L70-L75). The handler already has an outer HTTP middleware stack ([handler.go#L74-L80](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/op-service/rpc/handler.go#L74-L80)), but geth's `rpc.Server` dispatches by reflection with no upstream hook, so per-method/batch/websocket granularity is not free there.
- `rpc.JsonError`: [`op-node/rollup/engine/api.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/op-node/rollup/engine/api.go), [`op-test-sequencer/sequencer/seqtypes/types.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/op-test-sequencer/sequencer/seqtypes/types.go#L124-L139) (16 sentinel errors), [`op-interop-filter/filter/frontend.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1657fbe391d3f37785a6a3609422ee79fe86d9fa/op-interop-filter/filter/frontend.go#L28), `op-service/rpc/stream.go`, plus tests.

## PRs

1. **Own the recorder interfaces + client-side recording, and drop `rpc.JsonError`.** Define `Recorder`/`RecordedMsg`/`RecordDone` in op-service (no geth types in the signature) and move `RPCMetricer` onto them; implement recording in our own RPC client wrapper in `op-service/client` — a seam we already own. Replace `rpc.JsonError` with a local error type carrying the same `Code`/`Message`/`Data` and `ErrorCode()`, so JSON-RPC error codes on the wire are unchanged. Can land before the cutover.
2. **Server-side interception.** Design and build the replacement observation point — HTTP middleware that parses the JSON-RPC envelope, or wrapping the registered `rpc.API` services — and wire `op-service/rpc.Handler` to it. Metric **names and labels must not change**; per-message fidelity may be approximated (document what is approximated: batches, websocket, notifications).

## Acceptance criteria

- No monorepo Go file references `rpc.Recorder`, `rpc.RecordedMsg`, `rpc.RecordDone`, `rpc.WithRecorder`, or `rpc.JsonError`.
- The `<ns>_rpc_client_*` / `<ns>_rpc_server_*` metric names and label sets are identical before and after, verified by a test over the registered collectors.
- JSON-RPC error codes served by op-node engine API, op-test-sequencer, and op-interop-filter are unchanged.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5 (1M context)*

topIssues.title: contracts-bedrock: bump OPCMv2 to v9 and retire previous allowances
topIssues.author: 0xOneTony
topIssues.body:
PR https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22805 makes ETHLockbox deployment available during v9 upgrades. OPCMv2 still reports 8.0.4, so the allowance stays disabled until the version bump. The pre-v9 startingAnchorRoot override also needs to be retired.

Definition of Done:
- Bump OPCMv2 to 9.0.0.
- Remove the < 9.0.0 branch that permits overrides.cfg.startingAnchorRoot.
- Update upgrade callers and fork setup to stop supplying that override. Use the chain’s existing anchor root.
- Keep ETHLockbox deployment permission restricted to v9.
- Run the missing-lockbox upgrade tests against the actual OPCM version instead of mocking v9. Keep the version-boundary tests.
- Test the v8 → v9 upgrade on a fork, including chains with an existing lockbox.

topPRs.title: docs: publish the op-reth reference from gen-cli at v2.4.4 and retire the old CLI tree
topPRs.author: sbvegan
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #23102 (gen-cli); its diff shows that PR's commits until it merges.

The op-reth CLI reference is 73 pages under Node Operators › Reference, generated at v2.4.1 and three releases behind, with the same Logging and Display blocks reprinted on all 72 command pages and a 60-chain list on most of them, so a search for any common flag returns most of the tree (ethereum-optimism/solutions#1209). This replaces it with the first component on the generated, versioned reference the content guide specifies: 15 pages under `reference/op-reth/v2.4`, generated by gen-cli from the published `op-reth:v2.4.4` image in 13 seconds, with an index, one page per top-level command whose nested subcommands are headings, and a global-options page for the three sections every command repeated. The Reference tab now exists with the op-reth dropdown and its v2.4 version entry.

Effect on users: every old URL redirects. Nested subcommands land on the anchor of their heading (`db/checksum/mdbx` → `db#checksum-mdbx`), verified live with `mint dev` along with the root and overview redirects. The 69 older redirects that already pointed into the deleted tree are re-targeted so no redirect chains. The hand-written orientation page moves to Node Operators › Guides › Configuration ("Understanding the op-reth CLI"), since nothing under `reference/` is hand-written, and nine pages that linked into the old tree now link to the new one. The `op-reth node` page is 1,700 lines instead of the old tree's combined 17,700, and the chain list appears once, as a pointer to the superchain-registry. op-reth's flag catalog moves from three releases behind to current.

Effect on maintainers: `gen-op-reth-cli` is deleted; gen-cli regenerates this line with `--component op-reth --tag <tag> --image auto`, and `--check` verifies it. The nav, redirect, reference and link-policy lints pass on this branch with its own lint scripts (#23102 now carries the nav-lint change that understands `dropdowns`/`versions`, identical to #23091's, so this no longer waits on #23091). Until the tag-triggered regeneration job lands (ethereum-optimism/solutions#1518, Phase 2.2), a new op-reth release is regenerated by hand; the old tree had no working automation either (the README described one that was never registered), so this gap is not new.

Review: the deletion-reviewer agent swept the whole repository for references to the deleted URLs, nav group and generator, and verified one redirect per deleted URL, every anchored destination against the target page's headings, no chains, and no other generator or asset referencing the old tree. It found one dead link in `rust/UPDATING-RETH.md` step 9 of the reth-bump procedure (fixed), three descriptions that still said the reference was imported from the source tree or that subcommands get their own pages (fixed), and the nav-lint dependency above (resolved by carrying the change in #23102). No findings dismissed.

Redirect destinations name the `v2.4` line. When a new minor line ships and becomes the default, those redirects still resolve but land on v2.4; retargeting them is a one-line job for the regeneration workflow and is tracked with the versioning work rather than done here.

Refs ethereum-optimism/solutions#1518 (Phase 2, first migration); closes the collapse asked for in ethereum-optimism/solutions#1209. Depends on #23102 and #23091.

topPRs.title: kona-node: recover from RPC failures without cascading across chains
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
A transient L1 RPC failure in the watcher currently escapes as an actor error and shuts down the host, including unrelated chains. Simply logging and skipping the failed block is insufficient: if that block contains a signer rotation, the node can retain the wrong signer indefinitely. A closed derivation channel has the same excessive failure scope.

The broader problem is that recovery needs the semantics of the operation, not just the RPC. Configuration needs to converge to current state; engine work must survive outages without losing ordering; gossip becomes stale. A universal infinite-retry policy cannot distinguish these cases and can leave a shared actor stuck on one dependency.

The three commits address those levels. The watcher reads signer state from `SystemConfig` at the canonical head and retries failed reads, so missed rotations and reorgs converge without replaying every log. Engine operations retain pending work and retry with backoff; signing runs outside the network event loop with bounded attempts, allowing later payloads to proceed after an outage. Individual RPC deadlines bound stalls without cutting off healthy, long ancestry traversals. Independent per-chain watcher workers isolate slow RPCs, full queues, and closed channels; head updates can coalesce because consumers need the latest state. Losing every chain still terminates the watcher.

Added regression scenarios cover:

- Missed signer updates, recovery without a new head, same-height reorgs, and stale results arriving during an RPC or while the signer queue is full.
- L1/L2 reset failures, completion of the original reset request with a full derivation queue, long healthy resets, individual RPC timeouts, FIFO recovery of queued engine work, and signer failure followed by successful signing of a later payload.
- Healthy-chain head/finality/query progress while another chain stalls, chain-local channel closure, and cancellation of outstanding RPCs on shutdown.

304 affected-crate and downstream RPC tests pass locally. All CI checks and five required merge gates pass. Rust, recovery, reconciliation, and state-lifecycle reviews are complete; existing public error variants are retained for API compatibility.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22655

topPRs.title: op-service!: own the RPC recording seam and JSON-RPC error type
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
op-geth adds RPC recording hooks to geth's RPC client and server and exports `rpc.JsonError`. Upstream go-ethereum has neither, so `op-service/{metrics,client,rpc}` and every `JsonError` user would stop compiling at the cutover. They now build on an owned seam in the new leaf package `op-service/jsonrpc`:
- RPC metrics record through `jsonrpc.Recorder`.
- `op-service/client` records in its own wrapper around the geth client.
- `jsonrpc.Error` replaces `rpc.JsonError`.

With the `replace` dropped, `op-service/{jsonrpc,client,metrics}` type-check against upstream go-ethereum. The server side still uses op-geth's hook, but only in `op-service/rpc/server_recorder.go`. Replacing that is the second half of #22753. A forbidigo rule rejects the fork-only symbols everywhere else.

Operators see no change:
- **Metrics:** names and label sets are pinned by `TestRPCMetricsDescriptors`, and `TestServerRPCMetrics` checks server-side recording end to end. A differential test (not committed) showed the client wrapper records the same traffic as op-geth's hook, except for the `eth_unsubscribe` request that go-ethereum sends internally when a subscription ends. That request is no longer counted.
- **Errors:** JSON-RPC error codes on the wire are unchanged.

Smaller behaviour changes:
- op-test-sequencer now keeps the code of any wrapped `rpc.Error`, not only op-geth's `JsonError`. Before, other `rpc.Error` types were served as `-38501`.
- The conductor API clients in op-devstack and op-e2e go through `client.NewBaseRPCClient`, so they now get its default 10s call timeout.

BREAKING CHANGE: Go modules using these op-service APIs must update. `metrics.RPCMetricer.NewRecorder` returns a `jsonrpc.Recorder`, and `client.WithRPCRecorder` and `rpc.WithRPCRecorder` take one. Replace `rpc.JsonError` with `jsonrpc.Error`. `op-conductor/rpc.NewAPIClient` takes a `client.RPC`; wrap a `*rpc.Client` with `client.NewBaseRPCClient`.

Reviews: Go code review (it found a panic when closing a client with a live subscription, now fixed with a regression test), comment review, and test-coverage review (its gaps are covered by the two tests above). The op-claude security review runs before this is marked ready. Dismissed:
- Skipping the recording wrapper for `NoopRPCMetrics`. op-geth's hook also ran for no-op recorders.
- An `interop_checkAccessList` error-code test in op-interop-filter. That change is a type swap, and `jsonrpc.Error` serialization is covered generically.

Part of #22753.

topPRs.title: op-reth: fix reth v2.6.0 review findings
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
This fixes the blocking findings from my review of #23046. Each one is a regression that the reth v2.6.0 bump introduces. Stacked on #23046.

- **Isthmus withdrawals root:** with state masking on (the new default), an op-reth sequencer could write a wrong `withdrawalsRoot` into a block header, and a verifier could reject a valid block with `L2WithdrawalsRootMismatch`. The cause is upstream: `OverlayStateProvider::storage_root` ignored the overlay trie nodes. The fix lives in ethereum-optimism/reth#11, and this PR pins reth to that commit. A regression test, masked and unmasked over both storage versions, fails on #23046.
- **`op-reth proofs init`:** init now refuses a datadir whose state trie lags its tip, or where reth's repair of it was interrupted, which happens after an unclean shutdown or on a snapshot of a running node. Before, init seeded a proofs store that matched no block. With backfill, that then failed with `StateRootMismatch`; without backfill, the node silently served wrong historical proofs. The error tells operators to start the node once and stop it cleanly.
- **Block access lists:** `debug_getRawBlockAccessList` is no longer served. op-reth now refuses to start with `--rpc-cache.prewarm-bals` or `--rpc-cache.cache-computed-bals`: on OP, prewarming re-executes every block forever, and it feeds the untested block access list reconstruction into tracing.
- **Flashblock log stream:** `flashblock_receipts_stream` returns logs for filters with an address or topic again. Since the bump, it returned none for them.

**Before merge:** keep this as a draft until ethereum-optimism/reth#11 merges, then re-pin to the merged commit. The current pin is reachable only from the fork PR's branch.

**Not addressed:**
- Low-impact test-helper refactors suggested by the Rust review: a shared `RethTrieStorageLayout` conversion, named test tuples, and a network-args helper.
- A pre-existing issue: flashblock stream logs carry per-flashblock, hash-ordered `transaction_index`/`log_index`.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*
